You are reading a batch of messages from one Signal group chat. Your only job is to spot SLANG THIS ROOM HAS MADE ITS OWN — a word, abbreviation, or phrase used with a specific local meaning that an outsider would not get from a dictionary. This is NOT a transcription or translation task.

Do NOT report:
- ordinary Cantonese or English words used in their ordinary sense (係, 唔係, 好, OK, lor, la, thanks, ...);
- standard internet slang already in general use everywhere (lol, 笑死, yyds meaning its dictionary sense);
- anything you are not confident is genuinely used with a LOCAL, room-specific sense.

It is completely correct — and expected most of the time — to find NOTHING. Reporting an ordinary word just because a batch was given to you makes the output worse than empty.

For each genuine candidate you MUST point at the exact message it came from, by its numeric id from the list below. A candidate whose message_id is not one of the ids given is worthless and will be discarded.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object of this exact shape, nothing else — no prose, no markdown fence:
{"observations": [{"surface_form": "<as written>", "canonical_form": "<normalised form>", "sense": "<what it means here, in Cantonese or English>", "part_of_speech": "<noun/verb/adjective/interjection/...>", "message_id": <int, must be one of the ids below>, "confidence": <0.0-1.0 float>}]}
If nothing qualifies, respond with exactly: {"observations": []}
